output.title: Credential rotation is a workflow cost, not just a security topic
output.body:
If you run a small business, credential rotation usually shows up as plain workflow friction. Someone has to update an API key, SaaS password, or admin token, and a report, sync, or login stops working until it is fixed. The cost is not abstract. It is time spent noticing the break, tracking down what changed, and re-entering access in the right place.

AI is not the first thing I would reach for here. This is mostly a systems and access-management question, not a judgment-heavy one. You can use AI around the edges, for example to help draft an alert or summarise what changed, but the core work is still about how credentials are stored, updated, and checked. If the access handling is loose, clever tools just make the mess faster.

The bounded next step is simple: list the integrations and accounts you rotate manually today, then count how many times in a month someone has to re-enter or update a credential. Pick one recent failure and note how long it took to notice and repair. That gives you a real baseline for comparing manual work, a tooling change, or the choice to keep it human. Once you know that cost, the decision gets a lot less vague.
